name: Intralesional corticosteroid scalp injection
lead: Intralesional corticosteroid injection places a corticosteroid, most often triamcinolone, directly into patches of hair loss. Wikipedia's article on alopecia areata says steroid injections are commonly used where the hair loss areas on the head are small or where eyebrow hair has been lost [1].

A 2020 systematic review cited by Wikipedia reported more than 50 percent regrowth in 80.9 percent of patients treated with 5 mg/mL triamcinolone injections, while the same article notes that spontaneous remission makes treatment effects hard to judge, with up to 80 percent of people with one or two patches regrowing within a year without treatment [1].

paras: The procedure is used mainly for alopecia areata. Registered studies also examine it in central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (CCCA) [2].

A registered phase 2 trial combined Restylane and triamcinolone injections for alopecia areata (14 participants) [3]. A trial from 2009 compared intralesional botulinum toxin A with corticosteroid injection (20 participants, status unknown) [4]. Planned or recruiting trials compare topical calcipotriol with intralesional steroids [5] and intralesional triamcinolone with microneedling plus topical triamcinolone [6]. A phase 4 multicenter prospective study of CCCA treatments is recruiting [2]. Published results from these registrations were not found in the sources reviewed.

card.summary: Steroid injected into patchy hair-loss spots, mainly alopecia areata; reported regrowth is high but spontaneous remission complicates it.
card.note: Prescription procedure for alopecia areata; spontaneous regrowth is common in small patches.

quick.overview:
Small amounts of corticosteroid, commonly triamcinolone, are injected into patches of alopecia areata or eyebrow loss. It is a clinic-administered prescription treatment.

A 2020 systematic review reported over 50 percent regrowth in about 81 percent of patients at one concentration, though many small patches regrow on their own.
quick.mechanism: The steroid acts locally to dampen the immune attack on hair follicles in alopecia areata.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed do not detail side effects of the injections. Several registered trials are comparing them with other treatments.
